_comment: Tier 2 tests that fail on purpose, each pinned to a confirmed application defect rather than a rig problem -- see e2e/README.md's 'Known defects found by the suite' and each spec file's own header for the full mechanism. This file exists so a NEW failure is distinguishable from an expected one: scripts/check_tier2_failures.sh compares the actual set of failing Tier 2 test titles against this list in both directions, the same job Tier 1's known_failures does for 5xx routes. A new failure and a silently-fixed known one are both loud rather than being lost in 'the suite is red, as usual'.
_empty_is_the_healthy_state: The list is empty: every Tier 2 test passes, and any failure is a regression. Both defects that used to live here are fixed in application code -- the roll-forward classification defect (coa_sections built from the entity-TYPE template, never consulting EntityChartOfAccount) and the retained-profits identification defect that the first fix made visible (retained profits found by the numeric code 4199 alone, which a hyphenated MYOB/Xero chart never carries, so the year's result was closed into a synthesised 4199 line beside the entity's real equity account -- and reroll_forward_diff/_apply then reported, and would have written back, $20,000 of phantom drift once it wasn't). Pinned in core/tests_rollforward_classification.py and core/tests_rollforward_retained_profits.py. Do not add an entry here to quiet a red test: an entry is a claim that a specific application defect is confirmed and accepted for now.
